title: Sector playbooks: banks, IT, FMCG and cyclicals
objectives: Choose the key metrics for banks, IT services, FMCG and cyclical industries.
Explain why cyclical valuations mislead at the peak.
body_md:
## What to look at, sector by sector

| Sector | Key drivers and metrics |
|---|---|
| **Banks and NBFCs** | NIM, CASA ratio, loan growth, **GNPA / NNPA**, provision coverage (PCR), credit cost, capital adequacy, ROA, ROE, **P/B** |
| **IT services** | Constant-currency revenue growth, deal wins, utilisation, attrition, EBIT margin, rupee and dollar sensitivity |
| **FMCG** | **Volume growth**, price/mix, gross margin, input costs (palm oil, crude derivatives), rural vs urban demand, distribution reach |
| **Autos** | Volumes, average selling price, inventory days, commodity costs, EV transition capex |
| **Cyclicals (metals, cement, chemicals)** | Capacity utilisation, spreads, commodity price, debt, **EV/EBITDA** and P/B through the cycle |

## Banks are different

Debt is the raw material for a bank, so **EV-based multiples and free cash flow do not work**. Value banks on P/B against ROE and asset quality.

## Cyclicals trap

Earnings peak when the cycle peaks, so P/E looks **lowest at the top**. Use mid-cycle earnings or asset-based measures.

## Common sense checks

Compare each company with **peers on the same metric**, and with its own history. A metric without a peer is only a number.

> **Exam tip:** Banks: NIM, GNPA, CASA, P/B. Cyclicals: do not buy on a low P/E at peak earnings.
example: A steel company shows a P/E of 4 at record profits. An analyst using mid-cycle earnings gets a P/E near 12. The cheap look came from peak earnings.
say: For a bank I will check asset quality and P/B against ROE.
At the top of a cycle a low P/E is a warning, not a bargain.
never: A low P/E always means undervalued.

check.q: Which metric is most specific to a bank's asset quality?
Why can a cyclical stock look cheap on P/E at the peak?
Which valuation anchor suits banks best?
check.why: Banks are valued on P/B against ROE.
